title: Introduce lightweight toolchain bootstrap and quiet CI fastpath
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: CI feedback has become noisy and slow for incremental changes; developer iteration time suffers and ops noise spikes during large merges. This PR introduces a lightweight, deterministic toolchain bootstrap (small, cached build image + shim scripts) and a staged CI fastpath that quiets non-essential checks for path-scoped changes while preserving safety for integration and release lanes. Key goals: reduce noisy Green/Yellow cycles in PRs; speed up lint/test feedback for language-specific packages; make bootstrap deterministic and cacheable across self-hosted runners. Summary of changes: add a minimal toolchain docker image builder and published manifest; introduce `ci/toolchain/bootstrap.sh` and `ci/toolchain/README.md` that explain local dev shim usage; refactor GitHub Actions workflows into stage-aware lanes: quick-lint (fastpath), unit-test, integration, release-smoke; add path-aware triggers and a small premerge gating composite action that conditionally skips expensive jobs; consolidate node/python toolchains into a single `toolchain.yaml` manifest used by both actions and local shims; replace several legacy makefiles with taskfiles that wrap the shim; add a dependency-lock-checker step that validates `third_party/dep-manifest.json` on release lanes. Checklist: - [x] Add toolchain image builder and CI cache keys - [x] Replace legacy bootstrap scripts in services/* - [x] Migrate lint workflows to quick-lint fastpath - [x] Add path-aware gating composite action - [x] Add dev README and migration notes - [x] Run canary on infra repo and fix discovered flakes Backcompat/migration notes: Local developers should run `ci/toolchain/bootstrap.sh --local` once and optionally update their taskfile shortcuts; CI uses the new image by default and will fall back to previous runner setup for any job that opts out via `legacy_bootstrap: true`. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable opt-in on selected active repos for 48h, then flip default for all redwood services; monitoring: added a `ci.fastpath.skipped_jobs` metric and `ci.toolchain.bootstrap_latency` histogram. Related: ENG-1024 (ci noise); ENG-1107 (toolchain cache strategy).

Priya Nair: LGTm overall; request a stronger notice in dev docs about graceful rollout and how to opt out if runway failures occur
Aisha Patel: Added opt-out flag and explicit rollback steps to docs/dev/bootstrap.md; called out monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds
Marco Ruiz: Found a flake in python unit tests when using new shim image, added a suggestion to pin pip resolver in toolchain.yaml

release_notes: Introduced a cacheable lightweight toolchain and staged CI fastpath to speed up lint/test feedback and reduce noisy CI runs. Migration: developers should run ci/toolchain/bootstrap.sh once; ops will roll out staged lanes before flipping default.
summary: Adds deterministic, cacheable toolchain bootstrap, staged CI lanes with a quiet fastpath for incremental changes, and replaces legacy makefiles with taskfiles to improve DX and reduce CI noise.
